title: Collaborative aerial–ground warehouse inspection
description: A ground robot transports and localizes a UAV for short flights that capture imagery of warehouse shelves.
introduction: A ground robot can carry a UAV between warehouse aisles, reserving flight for close-range observations of high shelves. This collaborative system captures inventory imagery without external navigation infrastructure or a prior 3D map.

problem.heading: Combine ground endurance with aerial reach.
paragraphs: Ground robots cannot easily observe high shelves. UAVs reach those locations, but their battery limits make long transit flights costly.
Repetitive indoor aisles also make reliable localization difficult. The team needs navigation that can work with a simple floor plan.

approach.heading: Travel on the ground. Observe from the air.
paragraphs: The UGV combines 2D LiDAR scan-to-map matching with an Extended Kalman Filter. The UAV uses fiducial-based relative localization.
The UAV takes off, follows the ground robot, captures shelf images and lands. Ground transport connects these short flight segments.

evidence.label: Simulation evaluation
evidence.text: The paper compares ground-robot localization with established methods across simulated warehouse layouts.

evidence.label: Physical system trials
evidence.text: Real experiments demonstrate UAV following and landing, producing geo-referenced shelf imagery for downstream inventory recognition.

evidence.label: Data-capture scope
evidence.text: End-to-end item identification and enterprise-system integration are outside the paper’s scope.

sourceReferences: Primary publisher article and abstract: https://www.mdpi.com/2504-446X/9/11/792 (reviewed for this draft)
editorQuestions: No project-specific media is identified in the handoff. This draft is a text-only case study and does not borrow another platform’s footage.
Publisher source confirms simulation and physical following/landing; do not turn the image-capture result into a claim of demonstrated automated end-to-end inventory counting.
